nodes.title: How to use
widgets_values:
## LTX-2.5 · V2V · First/Last frame · IC-LoRA · SDR -> HDR · Native 4K/8K (subgraphs)

Same graph as `LTX-2.5_FLF_V2V_ICLoRA_SDR_to_HDR_Native_4K_8K.json`, packed into subgraphs.
Double-click a box (or its top-right icon) to open it; use the breadcrumb to go back.

**Left column - your inputs**: SOURCE video (yRead), FIRST frame, LAST frame.

**Boxes, left to right**
1. **Load Models** - every model file + LoRA strengths are widgets on the box.
2. **Prompt (stage 1)** - your prompt + negative. The HDR passes use the scene embeddings instead.
3. **Source + Sizes** - `output_size` 4K / 8K etc. The summary shows in *Tiling sizes*.
4. **Stage 1 - Generation** - FullHD, 8 steps, effect IC-LoRA + first/last frame guides.
   Saves an SDR FullHD preview (bypass that SaveVideo with Ctrl+B if not needed).
5. **SDR to HDR (FullHD)** - SDR-to-HDR IC-LoRA on the stage-1 result, scene embeddings, 8 steps.
6. **Upscale** - LTX latent upscaler x2 (x4 when output_size = 8K).
7. **HDR Refine** - tiled 3-step refine at 4K/8K with the **refine-details IC-LoRA** (as in
   Lightricks' HDR->HDR graph), guided by the decoded HDR-A result (ACEScct). Its widget is the
   look/detail prompt: keep it about look and sharpness, anything named stamps into every tile.
8. **Decode HDR** - decode (ACEScct) chained into ACEScct -> linear ACEScg. Its **ACEScg image**
   output (scene-linear AP1, no clamp) feeds **yWrite** (EXR) and **yViewer** on the right.
   No video is written at the end (only the SDR stage-1 preview).
   **Nuke**: read the EXRs as **ACEScg**, not ACEScct (they are linear, not log).

**Turning parts off** (select the boxes, then Ctrl+M = mute, Ctrl+B = bypass)
- *SDR FullHD only (no HDR, no 4K)*: mute **Decode HDR** + **yWrite** + **yViewer**. Nothing after
  stage 1 runs; the result is the Stage-1 preview (SDR FullHD).
- *HDR at FullHD (no 4K)*: bypass **Upscale** + **HDR Refine**. The FullHD HDR latent goes
  straight to Decode HDR.
- *SDR at 4K*: use `LTX-2.5_FLF_V2V_ICLoRA_Native_4K_8K.json` instead (here the 4K pass is HDR).
- *No yViewer*: bypass it (Ctrl+B); at 4K it stores ~5 GB of float16 frames per run.

**Rules**: euler sampler, overlap >= 0.5, `use_tiled_encode` off. Clip length 8n+1 frames
(97 / 121 / 161). Stage 1 renders the whole clip in one pass (keeps first/last pinned).
Models: see README in the repo (scene embeddings go in `models/embeddings/`). New for the 4K pass:
`ltx-2.5-22b-ic-lora-refine-details-1.0.safetensors` -> `models/loras/`
(huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5-22b-IC-LoRA-Refine-Details).

**yRead / yWrite / yViewer** (vfx_io + vfx_viewer)
- yRead: a MOV or an image sequence. With OCIO on, set *target colorspace* to your sRGB / display
  colorspace: stage 1 and the SDR->ACEScct step expect sRGB. `frame_grid` = LTXV (8n+1), pad.
- yWrite gets first_frame, fps, pad_frames and time_stretch from yRead. Its image is linear ACEScg:
  with OCIO on, pick your config's ACEScg for input and output (no conversion). Set root/folders
  in its panel, or switch destination to `path`.
- yViewer: colorspace_a = ACEScg (float16 keeps HDR values).

nodes.title: Downloads (GGUF Q6_K)
widgets_values:
## Downloads - GGUF Q6_K version

This copy loads the LTX-2.5 **distilled** model as a **GGUF Q6_K** file through
**Unet Loader (GGUF)**. Everything else is the same as the normal workflow.

**1. Custom node: ComfyUI-GGUF** (city96), via the Manager or:
`git clone https://github.com/city96/ComfyUI-GGUF` in `custom_nodes`, then
`pip install -r ComfyUI-GGUF/requirements.txt` with ComfyUI's Python.

**2. Diffusion model, GGUF Q6_K (17.8 GB)** -> `models/diffusion_models/` (or `models/unet/`)
`ltx-2.5-22b-distilled-Q6_K.gguf`
https://huggingface.co/unsloth/LTX-2.5-GGUF/resolve/main/distilled/ltx-2.5-22b-distilled-Q6_K.gguf
(repo: https://huggingface.co/unsloth/LTX-2.5-GGUF , folder `distilled/`)

**3. Text encoder, Gemma 4 12B comfy int8** -> `models/text_encoders/`
`gemma4-12b-with-proj-ltx-2.5-comfy-int8-convrot.safetensors`
https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5/resolve/main/text_encoders/gemma4-12b-with-proj-ltx-2.5-comfy-int8-convrot.safetensors
The int8 encoder is a ComfyUI safetensors file, not a GGUF, so it stays on the normal
**Load CLIP** node (type `ltxv`).

**Unchanged (same as the normal workflow)**
- Video VAE -> `models/vae/`: https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5/resolve/main/vae/ltx-2.5-video-vae-bf16.safetensors
- Latent upscaler x2 -> `models/latent_upscale_models/`:
  https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5/resolve/main/latent_upscale_models/ltx-2.5-latent-spatial-upscaler-x2-bf16-1.0.safetensors
- IC-LoRAs (and the HDR scene embeddings) as listed in the How to use note.

**Command line** (Lightricks/LTX-2.5 is gated: accept the licence on the page, then `hf auth login`):
```
hf download unsloth/LTX-2.5-GGUF distilled/ltx-2.5-22b-distilled-Q6_K.gguf --local-dir models/diffusion_models
hf download Lightricks/LTX-2.5 text_encoders/gemma4-12b-with-proj-ltx-2.5-comfy-int8-convrot.safetensors --local-dir models/text_encoders
```
`--local-dir` keeps the repo sub-folder (`distilled/`, `text_encoders/`): move the file up
one level, or pick it from the sub-folder in the loader.

**VRAM (RTX 3090, 24 GB)**: Q6_K is 17.8 GB vs about 22 GB for the int8 safetensors, which
leaves more room for the 4K/8K tiles.
